acceptance_criteria.criterion: configureUsers() performs only SELECT queries (no INSERT, UPDATE, or transaction start/commit) — it reads system user IDs via Application::getSystemUserIDs() and checks existence via AppFactory::createUsers()->idExists().

When any system user ID is missing from the test database, configureUsers() throws a BootException with error code 175001 and a message containing both the missing user IDs and the text 'composer seed-tests'.

seedSystemUsers() is public static, starts a transaction, runs the InitSystemUsers installer task, commits on success, and rolls back via DBHelper::rollbackConditional() on any \Throwable before re-throwing.
registerTransactionCleanupHandler() registers a shutdown function (via register_shutdown_function) that calls DBHelper::rollbackConditional().
_boot() calls registerTransactionCleanupHandler() between configureDatabase() and configurePaths().
The class constant ERROR_TEST_DB_NOT_SEEDED has an explicit int type declaration and value 175001.
All new code uses array() syntax (not []).

Replaced write-heavy configureUsers() with a verify-only implementation: iterates Application::getSystemUserIDs(), checks each via AppFactory::createUsers()->idExists(), throws BootException(175001) listing missing IDs with 'composer seed-tests' hint if any are absent.

Added private registerTransactionCleanupHandler(): registers a shutdown function that calls DBHelper::rollbackConditional().
All new code uses array() syntax (not []).
PHPStan --level=max: no errors. Test suite: 1098 tests, 7 pre-existing LDAP failures (missing config file), no regressions.

comments.note: configurePaths() uses die() on line 119 for a missing tests folder rather than throwing an exception. This is inconsistent with the rest of the bootstrap, which uses BootException. A low-priority improvement would be to replace die() with a BootException throw to allow callers (or shutdown handlers) to react gracefully.

The configureDatabase() method uses direct constant references (APP_DB_TESTS_NAME, APP_DB_TESTS_USER, etc.) without null-check guards. If those constants are undefined (misconfigured environment), PHP emits notices/deprecations in PHP 8+. Low risk in a controlled test bootstrap, but worth noting.

The existing configureDatabase() and configurePaths() methods use space-after-control-flow style (e.g., 'if ('), while the new configureUsers() follows the project's Allman brace style. Both are present in the file; the new code correctly matches the surrounding Allman style used in the class methods — no action needed.

summary: All 7 acceptance criteria verified by code inspection and test execution. PHPStan --level=max reports zero errors on the modified file. Two edge cases examined: (1) rollbackConditional() on shutdown is safely guarded by isTransactionStarted() — no risk of spurious rollback on a committed transaction; (2) configureUsers() silently passes when getSystemUserIDs() returns empty — acceptable per spec but noted as an observation.

comments.note: configureUsers() silently passes (logs 'System users verified.') when Application::getSystemUserIDs() returns an empty array. No users are checked, no exception is thrown. This is not a bug per the AC, but could mask a misconfigured system user list in future. Worth considering a guard like 'at least one system user ID must exist'.

DBHelper::rollbackConditional() in the shutdown handler is safely guarded by isTransactionStarted() — confirmed by reading DBHelper.php line 921. There is no risk of a spurious rollback after seedSystemUsers() commits successfully or when no transaction was ever started.
No new issues found — all 7 ACs fully met, PHPStan clean, no regressions. The 7 test failures are pre-existing LDAP ConfigTest failures due to missing test-cas-config.php, unrelated to this WP.
